scenes.title: Stone holds the morning
scenes.alt: Imagined scene of a small Odisha-style stone temple courtyard, with people passing in soft morning light.
scenes.scene: A quiet morning in a small Odisha Kalinga-style temple courtyard, weathered sandstone, one modest curving rekha-deul tower and low stepped-roof porch, no fantasy hybrid pagodas, no iconic monument claimed. A woman in everyday cotton sari passes through the foreground with a small flower basket, another visitor partly occluded behind a low wall, shoes outside precinct, a tree casts irregular shadows. Show the human scale and worn stone steps rather than an impossible grand palace. 35mm eye-level, a real off-centre view. Gentle natural morning sunlight, no sunbeams.

scenes.title: A story taking shape
scenes.alt: Imagined Pattachitra workshop: an artist paints a small detailed panel beside everyday working materials.
scenes.scene: Inside an ordinary Pattachitra artist's workshop inspired by Raghurajpur Odisha. An adult Indian artisan in a plain short-sleeved cotton shirt is seated naturally painting a small flat cloth panel with a fine brush; the panel has restrained traditional red, black, ochre and cream floral narrative motifs, no need for readable text or identifiable deity. Pigment bowls at hand, one unfinished panel leaning nearby, a pale plaster wall. Focus on concentrated profile, correctly held thin brush and the working panel. Side-window daylight, 50mm seated eye-level slightly above work, not top-down. No arranged souvenir shop, no piles of decorative props.

scenes.title: Threads remember
scenes.alt: Imagined handloom workshop: a weaver works with deep red and cream patterned cloth on a wooden loom.
scenes.scene: An adult Odia woman weaving at a working wooden handloom in a modest but cared-for Odisha weaving room. Practical cotton sari, attentive profile, yarns under plausible tension, a restrained deep maroon and ivory ikat/bandha patterned cloth emerges from loom. Show warp threads and her working position correctly; don't turn the loom into decorative timber or a modern knitting machine. Another spool and folded workcloth nearby for causal context. Soft open-door daylight. 35mm viewpoint diagonally across loom, face and emerging cloth as anchors. Real hands mostly naturally obscured by beam, no ornate costume or staged posing.

scenes.title: A meal that feels like home
scenes.alt: Imagined home meal centred on pakhala, with fried vegetables, greens and accompaniments on a simple table.
scenes.scene: An Odia home lunch being served. A wide steel bowl of pakhala with visible cooked rice submerged in lightly cloudy water is the central anchor; modest side plates of sautéed leafy greens, fried eggplant slices, crushed badi, green chilli and lime, not an elaborate pan-Indian thali. A serving hand entering from left with an ordinary steel ladle, two people only partly visible at table edges. Simple worn wooden table, naturally used kitchen setting, daylight from one window, 50mm three-quarter tabletop view. Food appetising and fresh, portions realistic; no dessert, no random floating flowers, no graphic labels.

scenes.title: Before the applause
scenes.alt: Imagined Odissi rehearsal: a dancer practises while a teacher watches from the side of a simple studio.
scenes.scene: An adult Odia woman rehearses Odissi in a plain airy studio in Odisha. Cotton practice sari draped for dance, feet bare, modest practice jewellery only, no elaborate stage crown. A plausible restrained tribhanga-inspired standing position, knees gently flexed, graceful arms not superhuman, hands naturally positioned. An older woman teacher seated at room edge observes quietly, no crowd. Open windows, simple floor with light wear, quiet natural daylight. 50mm full-body viewpoint at human height, enough floor for feet, realistic anatomy, no mirror reflections, no performance-stage spotlights.

scenes.title: Into the green quiet
scenes.alt: Imagined Odisha forest scene: a narrow path passes through leafy woodland in soft filtered daylight.
scenes.scene: A beautiful but plausible eastern Indian sal-dominated mixed deciduous forest, inspired by Odisha's forest landscapes, not an exact named trail. Narrow earthy footpath curves between irregular upright trees, leafy canopy, undergrowth patchy with open leaf-litter ground, a small ordinary stream glimpsed to one side. NO humans, NO tiger or exotic animals posed for camera. Bright overcast morning with soft filtered daylight, varied greens and moist earth, modest depth haze only if physically plausible. 35mm from standing on path. Do not make tropical rainforest, jungle fantasy, symmetrical avenue, ornamental moss coating every surface or golden light rays.

scenes.title: Where the morning opens
scenes.alt: Imagined southern Odisha landscape: cultivated fields sit below rounded green hills as people walk along a field path.
scenes.scene: Southern Odisha inspired rural landscape near Koraput: rounded green hills in middle distance, small irregular cultivated paddy plots in foreground, a footpath on bunds, a few red-tiled rural houses partly hidden by trees off to one side. Two distant adult people in everyday clothing walking along a bund to their fields, no portrait identification or tribal costume. Gently bright early morning with cloud patches, agricultural work ordinary and dignified. 35mm from slightly elevated village path, horizons plausible, no Himalayan peaks, no spectacular rice terraces from Bali, no plantation-resort imagery.

scenes.title: Colour is shared work
scenes.alt: Imagined Kotpad-inspired textile courtyard: two adults prepare reddish-brown yarn together beside dye vessels.
scenes.scene: An imagined everyday textile-work courtyard inspired by the Mirgan weaving and dyeing tradition of Kotpad in southern Odisha. Two adult Indian women in ordinary cotton saris work together handling wet reddish-brown cotton yarn beside a low sturdy dye vessel; one lifts a small skein with a wooden stick while the other sorts dried yarn. Off-white cotton and muted madder-brown yarn, simple useful vessels, a normal cared-for plastered house courtyard, practical working area. No costume pageant, no invented sacred ritual, no exaggerated jewellery, no identity claim for actual people. Natural late-afternoon light, 35mm candid oblique view, focus on collaborative work and interaction rather than a posed portrait. Yarn drips logically into vessel, no bare hand in boiling liquid.

scenes.title: A season for joy
scenes.alt: Imagined Raja festival moment: a young adult woman enjoys a garden swing while a friend stands nearby.
scenes.scene: An imagined Raja Parba celebration in a village garden in Odisha during the early monsoon. Two young adult Odia women in everyday festive cotton saris, one seated naturally on a simple rope swing suspended securely from one broad mango-tree branch, feet close to the ground; her friend stands at the side chatting rather than theatrically pushing. Quiet spontaneous laughter, a few leaves and modest handmade decoration on ropes. Swing connections and weight physically correct. Green garden after light rain, ordinary house wall partly seen, no crowded carnival. 50mm casual eye-level photo, soft daylight, no slow-motion flying fabric, no elaborate royal costumes.

scenes.title: A story finds its listener
scenes.alt: Imagined veranda reading circle: an older reader shares a book with two younger adults in soft daylight.
scenes.scene: An intimate Odia literary reading moment on a shaded veranda in Odisha. An older Indian woman wearing a simple cream cotton sari with a muted border reads from a small paperback to two young adults seated informally nearby, one listening with chin resting on hand. Books angled so all print is too small to read: NO invented legible Odia letters or titles, no recognizable famous author. One book spine, simple chairs, partly visible leafy courtyard, ordinary daylight reflected from wall. Candid 50mm viewpoint, not everyone looking at reader perfectly, gentle thoughtful mood, no nostalgic sepia filter, no staged school-photo arrangement.

scenes.title: Tomorrow is taking shape
scenes.alt: Imagined modern Odisha workspace: young adults collaborate on a small practical electronics prototype.
scenes.scene: Contemporary Odisha, an ordinary bright shared college maker workspace in Bhubaneswar, no identifiable institution. Three young adult Indian people, two women and a man, in natural everyday shirts and kurtas, collaborate on a small soil-moisture sensor prototype with a potted plant, simple electronics board, a laptop partly turned away and a notebook. One person adjusts a wire while a colleague checks the notebook, another listening, no posed celebration. Realistic modest practical equipment, clean but used table, open windows and leafy campus glimpse, cool white natural daylight. 35mm human eye-level, restrained believable work not futuristic sci-fi, no readable branding or screens, no corporate stock-photo grin.
